title: The Kings' Gate
journal: Never-Writes-Twice says the marked tower is one of the drowned spires off Lilmoth, and the divers of Bell Station will know which. This is the order's hunt; my own errand to Fort Chalkmoth may wait or come first. I'm to ask the steward of Bell Station, on an islet east of Lilmoth, which tower the stone marks.
objectives: Ask the steward of Bell Station which tower the marker stone shows. (marker: Meer-Tasi, Sees-Below)

plan.going: The order's hunt goes on; the marker stone's tower is a drowned spire off Lilmoth. My own errand to Fort Chalkmoth is open beside it.
plan.next: Ask the steward of Bell Station which tower it is.
plan.ways: Either order with Fort Chalkmoth; one way here, a question.

answers: I am hunting for the seven towers on behalf of the order (via Never-Writes-Twice). I gave her the Kings Marker Stone; she says the marked tower is one of the drowned spires off Lilmoth. The Unbound and the Collector Vanin are also after it.
Ask the steward of Bell Station (Meer-Tasi or Sees-Below, both quest markers) which tower the stone marks.
Talk to either person; Fort Chalkmoth is a side errand I could do first or later.
I do not know who the steward is of the two, what the Seal/Unbound plan is, or what moans in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar. I can find out by talking to people.

title: The Kings' Gate
journal: The steward, Meer-Tasi, knew the cut tower at once: Teku-Sul Spire, the drowned tower nearest Lilmoth, whose great gate her divers have never forced. The dive is long. I need a Hist's blessing, a spell or potion of waterbreathing (she sells them) or an enchantment, unless I am Argonian; inside the tower there is air. I'm to dive to Teku-Sul and find the great gate. The drowned priests' attendants walk its east halls; I may fight them or slip past.
objectives: Find the great gate deep in Teku-Sul Spire. (marker: Door to Teku-Sul East Halls, Door to Teku-Sul Halls, Ghost of Sul-Xeeth)

plan.going: The marked tower is Teku-Sul Spire, under the sea; its great gate has never been forced.
plan.next: Dive to Teku-Sul and find the great gate beyond the east halls.
plan.ways: Breathe by a potion (bought or brewed), a blessing, a spell, an enchantment, or being Argonian; fight the attendants, turn them with Restoration, or pass them by stealth.

answers: The stone marks Teku-Sul Spire, a drowned tower west of Bell Station near Lilmoth. Beyond its east halls is a great gate with three empty sockets, guarded by a priest ghost (Sul-Xeeth).
Get waterbreathing (Meer-Tasi sells potions), then dive to Teku-Sul and find the great gate.
Buy a potion, or use a Hist blessing/enchantment; sneak past or fight the priests attendants.
I do not know what the three sockets take, or why the Unbound want the gate; perhaps the ghost can tell me.

title: The Kings' Gate
journal: Before the great gate in Teku-Sul stands the ghost of a priest of the old kings, Sul-Xeeth. The gate has three empty sockets, one for each seal-stone the last king's priests cut, and only all three open it. One lies in the warden's vault at Blackrose Prison, one in the flooded vaults of Gemin, one in the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. I'm to tell Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka's House in Helstrom.
objectives: Tell Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka's House, Helstrom, what the ghost said. (marker: Never-Writes-Twice)

plan.going: The gate needs three seal-stones; I know where each lies.

answers: The gate in Teku-Sul needs three seal-stones set in its sockets to open it; it leads to the Root where the Hist roots meet and the Eye sits. Stones are at Blackrose Prison (warden vault), flooded vaults of Gemin, and deepest hall of Vorannuhl.
Report to Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka House, Helstrom.
Report now, or go after a stone myself; Fort Chalkmoth is a side errand.
I do not know what the Eye is exactly, or where Gemin, Vorannuhl and Blackrose are; the map or Never-Writes-Twice may tell.

title: The Kings' Gate
journal: Never-Writes-Twice made me a Reel-Ka, a Warrior of the order, and gave me its heavier armour, three hundred gold and a free bed in every Archwarden fort. Her orders are to take all three seal-stones before the Unbound do. I'm to fetch them from Blackrose Prison, Gemin and Vorannuhl, in any order; all three are marked, Blackrose the least dangerous and Vorannuhl the worst. My own errand to Fort Chalkmoth is still open.

plan.going: I am a Reel-Ka; the order wants all three seal-stones before the Unbound.
plan.next: Take the three stones from Blackrose Prison, Gemin and Vorannuhl, in any order (MN14 to MN16); Fort Chalkmoth is open too, my own errand.
plan.ways: Any order; the journal ranks them by danger.

answers: Notes for a friend picking up my save: The Kings Gate quest is done. Meer-Tasi at Bell Station named Teku-Sul Spire as the marked tower. The ghost Sul-Xeeth there said the great gate needs three seal-stones: one in the warden vault of Blackrose Prison, one in the flooded vaults of Gemin, one in the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. I reported to Never-Writes-Twice in Helstrom and became Reel-Ka (Warrior) of the Toh-Reel-Ka, got Reel-Ka Cuirass and Helm, 300 gold, free beds in Archwarden forts. Her orders: take all three stones before the Unbound.
Next: fetch the stones, Blackrose first (least dangerous), Vorannuhl worst; markers are on the map.

Any order; sneak is my preference. Fort Chalkmoth cellar errand (what moans there) is still open and Never-Writes-Twice dismissed it, which is suspicious. I still carry the Unbounds Recipe for the Seal, and about 1350 gold. I never needed waterbreathing; the game let me travel to Teku-Sul directly. Vanin the Collector is digging ahead.
Unknown: what the Eye of Argonia does when used, and what the Unbound want with it.
